requirements.requirement: The spec must define the quantization at the output boundary (dp per field, tie rule on fixed-point integers). It matters because: TS rounds money/shares to 2 dp and avg prices to 4 dp with JS Math.round (ties toward +inf); batch stats classify won/lost/flat by the sign of the ROUNDED pnl (pnl==0 counts as skipped even with trades; marketsPlayed = pnl!=0, not tradeCount>0 as the comments claim); and --extend recomputes segments from DB decimals, while a fresh run uses in-memory values. Emitted values must already be at or below the column scale, so a fresh run and an extended run cannot diverge. Parity must be judged on unrounded trace values: a 1e-6 internal difference can flip a 0.01 rounding and a win/flat classification.

requirements.recommendedDefault: Keep 2 dp, half-away-from-zero on fixed-point, in both profiles. Record ties that differ from JS as an intended difference in PARITY.md. Revisit 4 dp only together with a stats version bump.

requirements.requirement: Each Fill must carry its fee in USDC, computed once by ExchangeRules (feeSchedule by date, 5 dp rounding in the realistic profile). Portfolio cost basis and proceeds, marketStats.feesPaid and the simulator trace all sum fill.fee and never recompute it from a rate. Today three places recompute it independently from feeRateBps. pnl is already net of fees and fees_paid is informational, so any divergence silently breaks the pnl/fees relationship that protocols rely on.

requirements.requirement: Today one market job is a child of exactly one per-submission aggregate flow, keyed by idx; run-group returns N results and fails the whole group on any bad job. The spec must define: each candidate is its own backtest_runs row (own submissionUid, shared batch label); how group results reach the N aggregates; that each output echoes idx plus a candidate key; per-candidate failure isolation (a strategy error becomes that run's failure row, while data or IO errors retry the group); and how durationMs/eventsProcessed are attributed, since copying them to N rows inflates the per-machine leaderboard and durationTotalMs N times. A later --extend of one candidate runs standalone and must reproduce the group result.

requirements.requirement: Define how the worker supervises each binary. Set a wall-clock budget per job (scaled by events x candidates) and on timeout SIGKILL the binary's own process group. The binary exits when stdin closes or its parent dies (macOS has no PDEATHSIG). Exit codes are typed: 0 ok, 2 input (unrecoverable), 101 panic (deterministic, unrecoverable), killed by signal (OOM/jetsam: retry once elsewhere), 1 runtime (retry). Each result reports peak RSS and CPU time, stdout size is bounded, and fleet stray detection also finds native binaries.

requirements.requirement: Specify how a candidate group maps onto flows, jobs and rows. Recommended: one backtest_runs row per candidate under one group aggregate parent, because a BullMQ child can have only one parent. Each candidate gets its own submission_uid; candidates share batch_uid and a new candidate_group_uid. Each market job runs one market for a chunk of candidates. run-group returns an ok result or an error for each candidate, so one bad candidate does not fail the others. Every candidate run must be extendable on its own and give identical results.

Job size (markets x candidates) is chosen so that Redis round trips, spawn, sha verify and JSON stay under about 5% of compute, and a memory budget per slot bounds chunk size. The M6 benchmark reports fleet throughput (market-candidates per hour on 4 Macs), not only single-process speed.

requirements.requirement: The strategy crate template must ship a Cargo.lock derived from native/Cargo.lock, and every build uses `--locked`. The engine is reached by a path dependency into the sibling checkout, which workers self-update (fleet:git:pull / commit gate). requirements.requirement: The check gate must enforce determinism and candidate isolation with an engine-owned clippy config (CLIPPY_CONF_DIR set by the engine, so a protocol cannot weaken it). Global mutable state is banned (statics holding atomics/Mutex/OnceLock, thread_local!), because run-group runs N candidates in one process. Publish runs a smoke test: run-group of [p, p] and reversed candidate order on a fixture market must equal the standalone runs.

requirements.requirement: The spec must define what happens when strategy code panics or overflows. In TS, an exception fails that backtest market, while live logs it and keeps dispatching. In backtests, a panic produces a failure row for that candidate and market only, and the other candidates continue. Live behavior is explicitly chosen.

requirements.requirement: The spec must state which sample sizes ~$100 can reach and design probes with no directional exposure. Place/cancel latency: far-from-touch 5-share orders, about $0 cost, 2,000+ samples, enough to resolve p99. Taker path: $1-notional FAK round trips, about $0.045 per fill at p≈0.5, so ~500 taker fills for ~$25; enough for p90 and to detect a VWAP bias of ~0.1 tick. Maker: 5-share post-only bids on both outcomes, held as pairs; the cost is adverse selection, about $0.30 per fill, so ~100 fills for ~$30, giving the filled-share ratio to about ±20%; non-fill episodes are free and number in the thousands. Settlement timing comes free with every fill. Capital recycles every 5/15 minutes, so the binding limits are the loss budget and directional variance; pairs and round trips remove the variance.

missingAngles: Calibration is blocked by a dependency nobody covered. Live trading is disabled until the CLOB V2 signing and collateral migration is done (docs/live-trading/live-trading-bot.md:11, issue #249; package.json:190 still uses @polymarket/clob-client ^5.1.2). GOAL.md keeps the CLOB V2 adapter as stretch M8, 'NOT activated', and hard rule 8 forbids real orders. The ~$100 calibration therefore has no order path. The spec must state which stack places calibration orders and must change rule 8 to 'the agent never places real orders; the user may launch calibration'.

Live order-path failure semantics are missing. TS has no timeout, retry or rate-limit handling for order placement: only split and merge retry (LiveExecution.ts:617,751). The spec must define four things. (1) An ambiguous POST or cancel (timeout or 5xx) becomes an 'unknown' state that is reconciled from REST open orders and trades, with no blind retry that could double-place. (2) 429 and rate-limit backoff, and the exchange order and cancel rate limits. (3) One error-to-rejection-reason taxonomy shared by the live adapter and the simulator, so backtests can produce the same rejection classes. (4) Startup checks for account and region eligibility, plus close-only or market-closed states.

Live observability, alerting and process supervision are missing. No notification channel exists anywhere: there is no telegram/slack/ntfy in src, scripts or ops, and ops/swiftbar/polybot.mjs only shows fleet status from the dashboard. For real money the spec needs: alerts (kill switch tripped, session loss stop, WS data gap, heartbeat failure, reconciliation mismatch, strategy panic); structured logs with rotation; a launchd service for the live runtime like ops/macos/recorder-v4/*.plist.template (the trading bot has none); and an upgrade rule that the binary may only be swapped at a market boundary with no open orders.

The TS oracle keeps moving. Main has 18 commits touching src/trading, src/strategy, src/market and src/backtest in the last 60 days (post-only #252, batch cancel #254, capital #264, simulator #265, V4 integration). ts-compat parity is measured against a moving target. The spec needs: a pinned TS oracle commit per parity cycle; a rule that every engine-semantics PR on main adds an exerciser case or a PARITY.md entry; and a nightly parity canary on a Mac that has data. CI runs on ubuntu-latest (quality.yml:187) with no market data, so real-market parity never runs in CI.

Test infrastructure beyond trace parity is missing. Nobody specified invariant or property tests: cash plus reservations conserved, fills never exceed order size, reservations released on every terminal state, no negative positions in realistic. Nobody specified fuzzed event streams either: duplicates, out-of-order exchange timestamps, a price_change before the first book, crossed books, tick_size_change mid-market, empty sides. Small fixture markets must be committed so CI runs a full job end to end without R2 or DB. CI also builds x86_64 Linux while the shipped artifact is aarch64-apple-darwin, so the shipped target needs a macOS runner or a fleet canary.

There is no single source of truth for the TS/Rust contract. MarketJobData and RunSingleMarketOutput are mirrored by hand in TS types and Rust serde, and native.ts:151-172 does `JSON.parse(r.stdout) as TResult` with no validation. The spec needs: JSON Schema generated from the Rust types and checked in CI against the TS types; validation at the ingestion boundary, where an invalid output fails that market only instead of aborting the whole run's insert transaction; and an explicit unknown-field policy tied to jobSchemaVersion.

Input data contracts are not versioned. telonex_market_conversions has only a `converter` name and no format or schema version (src/db/schema.ts:503-525). The Rust reader hardcodes the TS converter's parquetjs column layout (native/crates/pmb-replay/src/telonex.rs:73, 441-443), so a converter change on main would silently break or mis-read native replays. Conversion rows and jobs need a format version that the reader can refuse. The job should also carry input integrity (etag or size, sha where it exists).

There is no rollback or run invalidation for engine bugs. Nothing defines a fleet-wide kill switch that disables native dispatch, a blocklist of known-bad engine versions enforced by workers and by the live start, or how runs produced by a bad engine version are flagged or quarantined in the dashboard and protocol evidence. This depends on the provenance columns but is a separate operational requirement.

Data retention and cost are not specified. backtest_run_markets is 5.73M rows / 7.58 GB and grows by +2.17M rows a week (finder measurements). Rust at ~6x speed plus candidate sweeps multiplies that. No retention policy exists for old runs, R2 native binaries, traces, fill ledgers or live journals. Live journals hold account data (order ids, wallet) and are calibration ground truth, so they need a private bucket and long retention.

There is no long-term policy for running two engines. GOAL.md:9-10 keeps the TS engine 'untouched' indefinitely, so every future engine feature must be built twice or the engines diverge. The spec should define the freeze or sunset policy, which engine is the default for new protocols, and how historical TS evidence is re-baselined once realistic numbers differ.

Market universe scope is not stated. GOAL never says which symbols and timeframes v1 must support. slug.rs parses eth, sol and 4h, Telonex also has 1h/4h/1d (src/config/telonex.ts:55), but fee and taker-delay rules, Binance pairs and Chainlink coverage differ per symbol, and Recorder V4 records BTC only, so calibration is BTC-only.

Supply-chain and publish authorization are not specified. The protocol sandbox can reach R2 (*.r2.cloudflarestorage.com in polymarket-protocols/srt-settings.template.json:67), so whoever holds sandbox R2 credentials can publish a binary that then runs on every fleet Mac, including the producer and live-key Mac. Nobody specified who may write strategy-artifacts/native/, or a cargo-deny/cargo-audit gate on the engine's dependency tree.

Success and kill criteria for the migration are missing. M6 asks only for 'report', with no speedup target, and no criterion says when to stop or keep TS. The user's question about the odds of live parity can only be answered against measurable targets: parity identity rate, fleet throughput multiple, calibration thresholds.

Docs and handoff material are missing. Nobody planned the VitePress pages (each needs a sidebar entry and must pass `npm --prefix docs run build`), CLAUDE.md updates (CLAUDE.md still names the removed rebuild:chunked-batch-stats), a Rust ENGINE-CONTRACT for agent authors per profile, or session-handoff rules so a fresh session can resume any milestone from STATUS.md alone.

Goal execution process is undecided. The WIP commit fef5f199 ('does not compile yet', 51 files, +9,953 lines including TS-side changes in backtest.ts and strategyArgs.ts) was built against a spec missing most of the requirements above: its portfolio uses HashMap, its TA plugin uses the OS libm, its feed latencies are read from env, and it has no ExchangeRules snapshot and no in-flight or delayed order states. Restart versus continue, the time-limit policy and user review gates were never decided.

openDecisions.question: Start the new goal on a fresh branch and worktree from the current main, or continue the rust-engine WIP branch?
options: Continue the WIP branch (fef5f199) and fix it until it compiles
Fresh branch from main, spec committed first. Freeze the WIP branch as a read-only reference and port only reviewed pieces (fixed.rs, slug.rs, the telonex reader, parity tooling, golden fixtures).
Fresh branch, ignore the WIP entirely
openDecisions.recommended: Fresh branch from main with the spec committed first. Keep the WIP frozen as a reference and cherry-pick only reviewed modules and test fixtures.
openDecisions.why: The WIP does not compile and was built against an incomplete spec (HashMap iteration, OS libm, env-read latencies, missing order states and rules snapshot). Main has also moved by 18 engine commits. Its fixed-point, slug and reader code and its TS-generated goldens are still useful test assets.

openDecisions.question: How is the autonomous goal bounded: a wall-clock limit (e.g. 10 h), per-milestone time boxes, or user review gates?
options: Global wall-clock limit
Per-milestone time boxes
No time limit; milestone proofs plus explicit user gates, with every milestone resumable from STATUS.md by a fresh session
openDecisions.recommended: No time limit. User gates after spec freeze, after M2 parity, before realistic becomes default, and before any real order. Each milestone ends with a demo command, a commit and a STATUS.md entry that a new session can resume from.
openDecisions.why: The user considers the 10 h limit unnecessary. The scope is multi-week, and decision gates prevent drift better than timers.

openDecisions.question: Integration strategy: one long-lived branch with a final PR, or incremental merges to main behind flags?
options: Single PR at the end; switch the fleet to the branch for M5
Incremental PRs to main: contract schemas, DB migrations, an inactive native worker shim and native queue, then the engine crates. Native dispatch disabled by default.
openDecisions.recommended: Incremental, inactive by default. The fleet never switches branch. If a switch is ever needed, use the pause-GR, drain, switch, test, switch-back, resume runbook.
openDecisions.why: GR daemons and pte run from the worker checkouts. Branch workers die on main-SHA jobs. Main changes weekly, and a 10k+ line PR cannot be reviewed.

openDecisions.question: What happens to the TS engine during and after the migration?
options: Keep evolving TS freely; re-check parity occasionally
Pin a TS oracle commit per parity cycle; every engine-semantics PR on main must add an exerciser case or a PARITY.md entry; after acceptance, freeze TS to bug fixes and build new features Rust-first
Delete TS after acceptance
openDecisions.recommended: Pinned oracle plus a parity-entry rule during the migration. After acceptance, TS is frozen to bug fixes, new engine features are Rust-first, and a sunset review is set for a fixed date.
openDecisions.why: A moving oracle makes ts-compat parity unverifiable, and maintaining two engines indefinitely doubles every feature.

openDecisions.question: Calibration needs real orders, and the TS live bot is blocked by CLOB V2 (#249). Which pieces move from stretch into core?
options: Keep the CLOB V2 adapter and Recorder V4 input as stretch; calibration is outside this goal
Promote Recorder V4 input only; calibrate later
Promote both: Rust CLOB V2 adapter (user-activated only) and V4 input as hard prerequisites of a calibration milestone
Fix TS #249 and calibrate with the TS bot
openDecisions.recommended: Promote both. Change rule 8 to: the agent never places real orders, and the user launches calibration with an explicit flag and a compile-time feature.
openDecisions.why: Client-side latency must be calibrated on the stack that will trade. Same-day calibration needs V4 (Telonex data lags 3+ days and has no trade prints), and fixing the TS bot would mean calibrating twice.

openDecisions.question: Which markets must native v1 support?
options: BTC 15m only
BTC 5m + 15m
Every symbol and timeframe Telonex has
openDecisions.recommended: BTC 5m + 15m guaranteed (parity, benchmark, calibration). Other symbols and timeframes are accepted when data and feeds exist, but are flagged 'unvalidated' in the run row.
openDecisions.why: Recorder V4 and calibration are BTC-only. Rules, feeds and Chainlink coverage differ per symbol.

openDecisions.question: What measurable criteria declare the migration a success, or stop it?
options: Report only
Explicit thresholds for parity, throughput and calibration
openDecisions.recommended: ts-compat: 100% identical order, fill and cancel sequences on the exerciser and lagsnipe.v15 over 200+ markets, with zero unclassified mismatches. At least 4x fleet throughput (market-candidates per hour on 4 Macs) on 1,000 markets (the earlier prototype measured 6.19x). Realistic becomes default only on the calibration thresholds. If mismatches stay unclassified after a full cycle, stop and report.
openDecisions.why: The user asks for odds of live parity. Only fixed targets make that verifiable.

openDecisions.question: Per-market money quantization in the output: keep 2 dp or switch to 4 dp (the column scale)?
options: 2 dp, half-away-from-zero on fixed-point, in both profiles (JS tie differences documented)
4 dp plus an explicit flat threshold in the TS stats and a stats version bump
openDecisions.recommended: Keep 2 dp, half-away-from-zero. Record the negative-tie difference from JS as intended in PARITY.md. Emitted values must already be at or below the column scale, so fresh and extended runs agree. Judge parity on unrounded trace values.
openDecisions.why: This keeps results comparable with every historical run. 4 dp changes win, loss and flat classification and needs a stats migration.

openDecisions.question: Should every result-affecting setting be stored as structured engine provenance per run instead of being re-parsed from the cmd string?
options: Keep parsing cmd

Indexed `engine` column ('ts' | 'native-ts-compat' | 'native-realistic') plus engine_version, engine_commit, binary sha and a versioned `model_config` JSON column (latencies, jitter, seed, gap thresholds, PTB latency, rulesVersion, fill model, per-market starting capital)
Fully normalized columns
openDecisions.recommended: Indexed `engine` plus `engine_version` plus a `model_config` JSON column, via a hand-written migration mirrored in the dashboard schema. The producer resolves ModelConfig and the job carries it, and the binary never reads env for behavior. The output echoes engineVersion, profile and seed, and TS asserts they match the request. Extend inherits and enforces equality. The dashboard flags comparisons across engines.
openDecisions.why: Worker .env files can silently change results today, a silent profile fallback is undetectable, and agents would compare TS, ts-compat and realistic numbers as if they were equal.

openDecisions.question: The dashboard Market Simulator and native runs: block them now, or have Rust emit the simulator trace format now?
options: Block native runs with a clear message (TS guard in resolveMarket)
Implement the simulator TraceSink in this goal
openDecisions.recommended: Block now. Make the simulator trace format a TraceSink in the milestone after parity.
openDecisions.why: Today a native run either throws or silently replays a TS registry strategy with the same id and labels it as that run.

openDecisions.question: Where are per-order and per-fill records and live per-market results stored?
options: Gzipped JSONL ledger in R2 per run and slug
New MySQL fill and order tables
Live and paper windows stored as normal backtest_runs rows with input_mode='live' or 'paper'
openDecisions.recommended: Opt-in ledger as gzipped JSONL in R2, plus live and paper windows as backtest_runs rows with input_mode='live' or 'paper', so live and backtest can be compared per slug with existing tools.
openDecisions.why: Calibration needs order and fill granularity. Adding a MySQL fill table to a 7.6 GB table set is expensive.

openDecisions.question: How are native market jobs gated and dispatched on the fleet?
options: Keep the producer git-SHA gate on the shared queue
Separate native queue; gate on worker shim version, protocolVersion, jobSchemaVersion and target triple; producer SHA and dirty flag kept as provenance only
openDecisions.recommended: Separate native queue with version and target gates. v1 is aarch64-apple-darwin only, and workers refuse other targets. Keep the commit gate on aggregate jobs and TS jobs.
openDecisions.why: The engine travels inside the hash-verified binary. The SHA gate forces branch switches and stalls the fleet on local branches.

openDecisions.question: Shared candidate replay: how is a group stored and attributed?
options: One run row with N candidates
N backtest_runs rows (own submission_uid, shared batch_uid, new candidate_group_uid and candidate_index columns) written by one group aggregate job
openDecisions.recommended: N rows written by one group aggregate, one transaction per run, idempotent per submission_uid. A candidate's strategy panic fails only that candidate; data and IO errors retry the market job. durationMs per candidate = group wall time / N, eventsProcessed = the full count, and every candidate gets the group's start and finish times. Each row's cmd is standalone-equivalent, and standalone --extend of one candidate must reproduce the group result.
openDecisions.why: Existing dashboard, protocol tools, extend and walk-forward all key on run id and params. The leaderboard and wall clock must not count compute time N times.

openDecisions.question: What is the group submission syntax, and what do execution-model variants and mixed feed requirements do?
options: `--candidates <file.json>` (explicit list, or {base, sweep, mode: coordinate|cartesian})
`--param-grid` inline
Mixed feed requirements: reject
Mixed feed requirements: split automatically into sub-groups
openDecisions.recommended: `--candidates <file.json>`. Reject duplicate normalized params and mixed feed or eligibility requirements in v1. Also allow candidates that differ only in ModelConfig (fill model, queue parameter, latency calibration id) for internal calibration and A/B use. One shared per-market seed derived from (run seed, slug).
openDecisions.why: Calibration and the realistic A/B reports need execution variants on one market read. Mixed feeds change the eligible universe.

openDecisions.question: Should sweep results store per-market rows for every candidate, or only for the best ones? What retention policy applies to old runs and artifacts?
options: Full per-market rows for every candidate
Segments for all candidates; per-market rows only for the top-5 and promoted candidates (others re-run on demand)
Plus a retention policy (e.g. drop market rows of unpromoted runs older than N days; keep segments)
openDecisions.recommended: Segments for all, rows for the top-5 and promoted, results moved out of Redis as chunks finish, a hard cap on candidates x markets per group, and a retention policy for unpromoted runs, R2 traces and ledgers. Live journals are kept long-term in a private bucket.
openDecisions.why: 100 candidates x 5.5k markets is about 6.6 GB of Redis on a 16 GB Mac, and the DB already grows by 2M+ rows a week.

openDecisions.question: Will sandboxed Global Runtime agents write Rust strategies in this goal, and which dependencies may strategy crates use?
options: Yes, built inside the sandbox (vendored crates, offline)
Yes, built in a step outside the sandbox
Not in this goal (only the implementation session builds, on m1-ivan)
Crates: free choice / only SDK re-exports
openDecisions.recommended: Not in this goal. Design a build step outside the sandbox now (shared target dir per machine, capped -j). Strategy crates use only SDK re-exports, with no extra crates.
openDecisions.why: The sandbox blocks crates.io and ~/.cargo, and GR hosts run 8 backtest slots. Extra crates break offline builds and add nondeterminism (rand, wall clock).

openDecisions.question: Artifact identity and trust: is the sha of a binary built on any machine acceptable, and what must hold before the live runtime loads a binary?
options: Binary sha from any machine plus a source_hash for dedupe
Only one canonical builder publishes
Live requires a clean recorded commit, engine at or above the live-safe minimum, and a verified reproducible rebuild to the same sha
openDecisions.recommended: Any machine with path remapping (--remap-path-prefix, pinned toolchain, --locked, one profile, ad-hoc codesign after strip), identity = binary sha, plus source_hash, target, rustc and engine commit columns. Live requires a reproducible rebuild from a clean commit that matches the sha.
openDecisions.why: A test build contained 74 absolute /Users paths. A binary cannot be reviewed the way a 30 KB TS bundle can, so a reproducible rebuild is the only way to review it.

openDecisions.question: Which build profile do strategy artifacts use?
options: Fast: lto=false, codegen-units=16, panic=unwind, overflow-checks=true
Current: thin LTO, cgu=1
openDecisions.recommended: Fast profile for check, iterate and publish alike. Revisit only if the M6 benchmark shows replay CPU rather than parquet IO dominates.
openDecisions.why: Measured warm rebuild 0.84 s vs 7.3 s. catch_unwind requires unwind, and overflow checks guard the fixed-point money math.

openDecisions.question: Plugin scope of the first SDK release, and how TechnicalIndicators works when it is ported.
options: Port all five plugins now
Ship ExternalFeeds, DwellGate and TimeWindowGate; defer TA and Volatility
TA candles from local Binance aggTrades files
TA strategies stay on the TS engine
openDecisions.recommended: Ship the three plugins that active authors use. When TA is ported, build candles from local aggTrades (extended preflight lookback), with no network calls inside the binary.
openDecisions.why: Only inactive SplitSellRedeem.v5.x uses TA and Volatility, and TS TA fetches REST klines with a wall-clock wait, which is nondeterministic.

openDecisions.question: Should a Rust port of a TS strategy keep the TS id, or get a distinct one?
options: Same id, distinguished only by the engine column
Distinct id (e.g. `overnight-opus55-lagsnipe.v15.rs`)
openDecisions.recommended: Distinct id, and also store the engine and profile on the run row.
openDecisions.why: The dashboard and protocol tools group by `strategy`, so a shared id would mix engines.

openDecisions.question: Where do backtests get per-market ExchangeRules (tick, min size, fee schedule, taker delay, negRisk, version), and what happens when a snapshot is missing?
options: Dated rules table compiled into the engine
Per-market snapshot (raw Gamma plus CLOB market JSON) stored per condition_id by a backfill, plus V4 rawJson
Missing snapshot: dated fallback with a flag
Missing snapshot: skip the market
openDecisions.recommended: Snapshot table per condition_id (producer backfill plus V4). Use the dated fallback when it is missing, marked rulesSource=fallback. tick_size_change events override in force. rulesVersion travels in the job and is stored on the run. Aggregation does not pool across fee eras.
openDecisions.why: telonex_markets has no rules columns, and the Rust rules are hardcoded and marked 'not verified'.

openDecisions.question: When the docs and observed data disagree on a fee era (formula, rate, start date), which one wins?
options: Docs
Charged amounts (on-chain fills or Data API usdc_size)
openDecisions.recommended: Charged amounts. Update the dated table and docs/polymarket/index.md to match. Realistic cannot become default until a sample from every era matches to the rounding unit.
openDecisions.why: The docs and Rust already disagree on era 1, era 2 and the boundaries, and WS fee_rate_bps was 0 on every print in a fee-charging era.

openDecisions.question: In the realistic profile, what happens to resting orders and in-flight intents at the end of the window, and may plugins see pre-window ticks?
options: Copy TS (everything freezes at the window edge)
Strategy called only inside the window; keep matching already-submitted orders until endMs, then expire everything; plugins observe pre-window ticks without strategy calls
openDecisions.recommended: The second option, applied identically to every input mode, the simulator and live.
openDecisions.why: TS gates differently per mode (V4 not gated, while the simulator gates V4), so backtest, simulator and live disagree today.

openDecisions.question: Research backtests over markets we traded live: use books with our own orders removed, or leave those markets out?
options: Use de-contaminated books everywhere
Exclude own-activity markets from research
De-contaminated for calibration; excluded from research universes by default
openDecisions.recommended: De-contaminated for calibration. Exclude own-activity markets from research by default, and flag them in the catalog.
openDecisions.why: Our own prints would otherwise count as market flow and fill the simulated order a second time.

openDecisions.question: Who sends split, merge and redeem transactions in the Rust live runtime?
options: Rust (alloy plus a relayer port)
TS sidecar called through an async request and response
openDecisions.recommended: TS sidecar for the on-chain tx. Rust models split and merge as async operations with latency and success or failure events, identical in paper and backtest.
openDecisions.why: The relayer SDK exists only in TS, and the core must not block on chain calls.

openDecisions.question: Live journal format?
options: New ad-hoc JSONL
Recorder V4 envelope (schemaVersion 4) extended with account, REST, timer and operator-command sources, plus an execution sidecar
openDecisions.recommended: The extended V4 envelope, with a minimal V4/journal reader in the paper-mode milestone. Journal raw frames, rules, REST request and response pairs with send and ack times, clock-offset samples, binary sha, params, profile and seed.
openDecisions.why: One Rust reader then replays both worker-2 recordings and live journals, and journal replay is the M7 proof.

openDecisions.question: Which clock drives ctx.now in live and recorded or journal replay?
options: Exchange timestamp
Local receive time, with the exchange timestamp exposed separately
openDecisions.recommended: Local receive time whenever the input has it (Telonex keeps the exchange time). GTD and expiry are checked against the estimated exchange time (local minus measured skew), and the skew is journaled at startup.
openDecisions.why: Today live mixes exchange timestamps and Date.now(), and the Rust tick has no rule for which one drives decisions.

openDecisions.question: Rust paper mode: simulate fills, or record decisions only?
options: Simulate fills with the realistic profile
Decisions only, like the TS dry-run
openDecisions.recommended: Simulate fills with the realistic profile; decision-only mode as a flag.
openDecisions.why: The TS dry-run never fills, splits or expires orders, so it is useless as a reference.

openDecisions.question: At startup or after a crash, what happens to open orders and positions from a previous instance in the current market?
options: Cancel orders and adopt positions read-only (flagged)
Adopt orders and positions
openDecisions.recommended: Cancel (cancel_market for the current condition ids), journal it, adopt positions read-only and flag them.
openDecisions.why: Strategy state is lost on restart, so adopted orders would be invisible to the decision logic.

openDecisions.question: Turn on the CLOB heartbeat dead-man switch, and enforce a single owner per API key?
options: Heartbeat off
Heartbeat on in real-order mode only, with a lockfile enforcing one process per key
openDecisions.recommended: On in real-order mode only, with one owner per key enforced by a lockfile. Paper mode never sends heartbeats. Heartbeat-caused cancels map to order_done with a cause.
openDecisions.why: Heartbeats are chained per key, and a missed one cancels all of that user's orders, including another bot's.

openDecisions.question: What is live available cash?
options: Virtual 500 USDC per market (as in TS)
min(configured per-market allocation, CLOB collateral balance minus reservations across all still-open markets)
openDecisions.recommended: The min() rule. Backtests keep isolated per-market capital equal to the same allocation. Also add session-level guards that do not reset on market rotation (session loss including settlement, wallet exposure, order-rate cap, kill switch), and fills are never dropped.
openDecisions.why: A $100 wallet partly locked in unredeemed markets cannot back a 500 USDC virtual budget.

openDecisions.question: Live behavior when the strategy panics (backtest: candidate-level failure row)?
options: Skip that callback and continue (TS behavior)
cancel_all for that market, stop calling the strategy until the next rotation, alert
openDecisions.recommended: cancel_all, halt until rotation, alert.
openDecisions.why: Continuing with a strategy whose state is corrupt while orders rest is the riskiest option.

openDecisions.question: Which alert channel does the live runtime use?
options: macOS notifications or SwiftBar only
Phone push (Telegram bot or ntfy)
Email
openDecisions.recommended: Phone push plus a SwiftBar status line. Alert on kill switch, session loss stop, WS gap over a threshold, heartbeat failure, reconciliation mismatch, strategy panic and rejected-order bursts.
openDecisions.why: No alerting exists today, and an unattended live run with real money needs one.

openDecisions.question: How is the ~$100 calibration budget split, and what loss stops the run?
options: Equal split
Rules and latency $5 / taker $25 / maker $30, stop at $60 cumulative loss, over 2-4 days of worker-2-recorded BTC 5m/15m markets
openDecisions.recommended: $5 / $25 / $30 with a $60 stop. Day 0 is rules probes (GTD lead, taker delay, tick, minimum sizes, post-only, batch cap), using non-marketable or $1 orders.
openDecisions.why: Paired or round-trip probes remove directional variance, so loss budget and sample size are the binding limits.

openDecisions.question: Which frozen pass thresholds make `realistic` the default profile?
options: Judgment after looking at results
Pre-registered thresholds frozen before the live run
openDecisions.recommended: Accept/reject agreement >= 99%. Fee error 0 at 1e-6 USDC. FOK/FAK agreement >= 95%. At least 90% of taker fills at the same VWAP, with mean |error| <= 0.25 tick. Maker filled-share ratio within [0.8, 1.25] at 95% CI. Median time to fill within ±30%. Per latency component: |median bias| <= 10 ms and p90 within ±20% (n >= 200). Pinned PnL error <= 0.5 cents per share, with a CI containing 0. The result applies only within the calibrated validity envelope (sizes up to ~10 shares, BTC, that host).
openDecisions.why: Pre-registration prevents moving the goalposts, and $100 cannot validate size effects or edge.

specOutline: native/spec/00-README.md: Index and reading order for a fresh session. Glossary (profile, candidate, group, ExchangeRules, ModelConfig, journal, ledger). How spec, DECISIONS, STATUS and PARITY relate. The hard anti-drift rules (idiomatic Rust, no JS emulation, TS = behavior oracle, not a bug spec). Handoff rule: every milestone must be resumable from STATUS.md alone.

native/spec/01-scope-milestones.md: Replaces GOAL.md. Objective and the Rust/TS ownership boundary (backtest and live). Market universe for v1. Out-of-scope list. Milestones with proof commands and user gates: spec freeze, core, ts-compat parity, realistic profile, candidate groups, artifacts and fleet, benchmark, paper live plus V4 input, CLOB V2 adapter (user-activated), calibration. Success and kill criteria. TS oracle pin and drift policy. Incremental merge-to-main strategy with native dispatch off by default. Amended rule 8 (no agent real orders; user-launched calibration allowed).
native/spec/02-decisions.md: Decision log: every open decision with options, chosen answer, date and rationale. A fresh session treats anything unresolved here as blocking and never improvises.

native/spec/10-domain-model.md: Fixed-point types (Price, Qty, Usdc, 1e6 base), the rounding direction for every operation, and the output quantization rule (2 dp half-away-from-zero, ties documented). Outcome and asset indexing. Ids (clientOrderId rules). The clock model: exchange ts vs local receive ts, which clock drives ctx.now per input mode, skew estimation. Determinism rules: no HashMap iteration in decisions, pure-Rust libm, seeded RNG from (run seed, slug) only.

native/spec/11-exchange-rules.md: ExchangeRules fields (tick, min size per order type, price bounds, fee curve and feeSchedule, taker delay, GTD lead and early expiry, batch cap 15, negRisk, exchange version v1/v2, minimum order age). Sources: per-condition snapshot table, V4 rawJson, dated fallback with rulesSource. Fee-era table with charged-amount evidence. tick_size_change handling. Per-rule verification status, set by the probes.

native/spec/12-engine-core.md: Single serial event loop and input envelope (seq, mono and wall receive times). Intents and validation. Order state machine (in-flight, delayed, live, matched, terminal; unknown on ambiguous REST). Settlement statuses (MATCHED, MINED, CONFIRMED, FAILED reversal) and sellable inventory. Capital reservation. Portfolio and cost basis, with the fee taken from fill.fee only. Cascade semantics and limits, without dropping fills. Strategy lifecycle per market. Window-gate rule per input mode. catch_unwind fault semantics for backtest, group and live.

native/spec/13-execution-models.md: Execution trait (simulator, paper, CLOB V2). The ts-compat quirk-flag list. Each realistic fix with its A/B report requirement. FillModel options: worst-queue, queue-position with the calibrated cancel-ahead parameter, partial maker fills. LatencyModel as named seeded quantile tables per component (market data, send, place resting and marketable incl. taker delay, cancel, ack, user-WS fill delivery, MINED/CONFIRMED, split/merge). Discrete-event scheduler firing at exact event times. Async split and merge model. Removal of our own orders from recorded books.

native/spec/14-feeds-and-plugins.md: Binance aggTrades, Chainlink two-clock and PTB visibility models with their parameters coming from ModelConfig, never env. Data-gap and coverage errors classified retryable vs fatal. Synthetic feed ticks. v1 plugin set (ExternalFeeds, DwellGate, TimeWindowGate) with math references and golden fixtures. Deferred TA and Volatility, with the offline-candles rule. No network I/O inside plugins or the binary.

native/spec/15-inputs.md: telonex-delta reader contract with a converted-parquet format version (new column plus job field; reader refuses unknown). Recorder V4 reader: manifest and sha verification, coverage gate, incomplete_capture, --allow-capture-gaps, receipt order. Live journal reader. TS resolves every input to a verified local file before spawn. Data-anomaly policy (duplicates, out-of-order, missing first book, crossed books), with each case counted in diagnostics.

native/spec/20-binary-protocol.md: Replaces BINARY-PROTOCOL.md. Subcommands describe, run, run-group, paper and live. The describe capabilities block (inputModes, profiles, protocolVersion, jobSchemaVersion, engineVersion and commit, sdkVersion, toolchain, target, JSON Schema of params). Typed exit codes (0 ok, 1 retryable runtime, 2 invalid input, 3 data-unavailable retryable, 101 panic) and a one-line stderr reason. Stdin and parent-death exit. Env allowlist and secrets-by-fd rule. Live and paper state stream plus operator command channel bound to 127.0.0.1.

native/spec/21-job-and-output-contract.md: MarketJobData, including the ModelConfig, rules snapshot, worker identity, candidates list and input integrity. RunSingleMarketOutput field by field. Null-vs-zero-row and skip taxonomy. Closed vocabularies and finite numeric ranges per DB column. intentMeta construction (fill order, dedupe by clientOrderId, size cap). eventsProcessed and eventsByType semantics. Echoed engineVersion, profile and seed. Per-candidate ok-or-error results. JSON Schemas generated from Rust and checked in CI against the TS types. TS ingestion validation, where an invalid output fails that market only.

native/spec/22-trace-ledger-journal.md: Canonical parity trace (TRACE.md content). Opt-in per-market order and fill ledger (gz JSONL in R2 keyed by run and slug). Dashboard simulator trace format as a future TraceSink, plus the v1 native-run guard. Live journal schema: extended V4 envelope plus an execution sidecar with send, ack and match times, transaction hashes, status progression and clock-offset samples. Redaction rules (no secrets).

native/spec/30-strategy-sdk.md: Curated, semver'd pmb-sdk prelude. Intent builders with free-form JSON meta. Price, Qty and Usdc newtypes with explicit tick rounding. Typed market times. Params derive (defaults, string coercion, unknown-key rejection, flatten composition, idempotent normalization, JSON Schema export, feeds and plugins computable from params). Leveled logging, off by default on the fleet. Engine-owned clippy and lint config for determinism and candidate isolation. Testkit and local single-market run. Example strategy. Rust ENGINE-CONTRACT text for agent authors, per profile.

native/spec/31-artifacts-build-publish.md: Crate layout (one package per protocol, one bin per strategy version) and gitignore of target/. Pinned toolchain, Cargo.lock derived from native/, --locked --offline. Canonical build flags (path remap, fast profile, panic=unwind, overflow-checks, ad-hoc codesign after strip, deployment target). source_hash and strategy_artifacts columns (kind, target, rustc, engine commit, lock hash). R2 keys. Publish authorization. Dedupe. Rebuild-from-source command. Live trust gate. Local cache LRU and prefetch. Out-of-sandbox build step design for later agent use.

native/spec/40-fleet-integration.md: Native queue and the version and target gate. Worker shim supervision: wall-clock budget scaled by events x candidates, process-group kill, peak RSS and CPU reporting, bounded stdout. Execution stamping by TS (machineId, slot, timing, worker sha). Slot and thread accounting and job granularity. Env allowlist plus sandbox-exec deny-network profile. Fair scheduling across submissions. Kill switch to disable native dispatch. Engine-version blocklist. Cross-machine determinism proof (same jobs on 4 Macs, byte-identical output). Runbooks: deploy, rollback, pause-drain-switch.

native/spec/41-candidate-groups.md: --candidates file format (explicit list or sweep spec, coordinate or cartesian; execution-model variants for internal use). Producer flow: describe each candidate, reject duplicates and mixed feeds, select markets once, print a candidate-to-submissionUid map. Shared-context job shape. BullMQ mapping with one group aggregate writing N runs idempotently. Failure isolation. Duration attribution. Redis offload and caps. Storage tier (top-N rows). Standalone-extend equivalence. M4 proof on persisted DB rows via verify-backtest-diff.

native/spec/42-persistence-and-stats.md: DB migrations, hand-written and mirrored in dashboard/src/lib/schema.ts: engine, engine_version, model_config, seed, candidate_group_uid and index, strategy_artifacts kind and target, rules snapshot table, conversion format version. What TS keeps computing (segments, batch stats, wall clock, failures, extend merge). The invariant that segments are recomputable from per-market rows. Dashboard changes (engine badges, refusal to compare across engines). Live and paper results as runs. Retention policy for rows, traces, ledgers, binaries and journals.

native/spec/50-live-runtime.md: Ownership split (Rust core vs TS sidecars for approvals, redeem, split/merge tx, WebUI). Discovery, pre-subscription and rotation. Resolution tracking per finished market. Reconnect and startup reconciliation with text PING. CLOB V2 specifics (version-selected asset ids, signing domain, order struct, collateral asset types). REST failure semantics (ambiguous outcomes, 429 backoff, error taxonomy shared with the simulator). Heartbeat ownership and lockfile. Live capital source. Session risk guards and kill switch. Real-order gate (CLI flag plus compile feature, never DRY_RUN). Secrets handling. Alerting channel and triggers. launchd service and an upgrade rule at market boundaries only.

native/spec/51-calibration-plan.md: Prerequisites (CLOB V2 adapter, V4 input, journal). Day-0 rules probes. Probe designs and budget split with stop-loss. Host isolation (stop or cap workers and GR on the bot host and worker-2). Join with V4 by condition_id, transaction_hash and book hash, with a measured clock offset. Own-fill attribution and wallet reconciliation. Removal of our own orders from recorded books. Execution-pinned harness (mode A) vs end-to-end determinism replay (mode B), with neutrality and sensitivity self-tests. Pre-registered metrics and thresholds. Calibration artifact versioning and its validity envelope (what $100 cannot calibrate). Re-calibration cadence.

native/spec/60-verification.md: PARITY.md classification rules and the pinned TS oracle. Exerciser spec (EXERCISER.md content) plus required cases for every engine-semantics change on main. lagsnipe.v15 parity set. Invariant and property tests, and fuzzed anomaly streams. Committed fixture markets for CI. CI matrix (ubuntu checks plus a macOS or fleet canary for the shipped target). Nightly real-market parity canary. Benchmark methodology (fleet throughput, same 1,000 markets) and acceptance targets.
